children: Goldman Sachs couldn't make up its mind. In the span of four days around September 15-16, 2026, the bank flipped its Federal Reserve forecast twice, moving from a prediction of a single isolated rate hike to anticipating a second increase as soon as October.

The catalyst was the Federal Reserve's September 16 FOMC meeting, where the central bank raised its target interest rate by 25 basis points to a range of 3.75%-4.00%. That marked the Fed's first rate increase since 2023.

Going into the meeting, Goldman's base case was relatively tame. The bank expected a 25-basis-point hike but characterized it as a one-and-done move, an isolated recalibration rather than the start of a new tightening cycle.
Then the Fed released its dot plot, and the mood shifted fast. Sixteen out of 18 policymakers indicated they expected at least one additional rate increase before year-end.

Goldman responded by scrapping its isolation thesis and pivoting to forecast another hike in October. CME FedWatch pricing moved in lockstep, with market-implied odds of a 25-basis-point October hike climbing above 50% following the announcement.
Bitcoin's immediate reaction was surprisingly calm. The leading cryptocurrency traded at approximately $76,000 after the announcement, posting a modest gain of about 0.5%.

The mechanism is straightforward. Higher interest rates pull liquidity out of the financial system. When cash earns a meaningful yield sitting in Treasuries or money market funds, the opportunity cost of holding volatile, non-yielding assets like Bitcoin and XRP goes up.
Bitcoin's track record during prior tightening cycles bears this out. During the 2022-2023 rate hike campaign, Bitcoin fell from near $47,000 to below $16,000 before recovering.

Bitcoin's resilience in the immediate aftermath of the September hike offers a counterpoint. A 0.5% gain on a day the Fed raised rates for the first time since 2023 suggests the September hike itself was largely priced in before it happened.

With 16 of 18 Fed officials signaling at least one more hike this year, the question of whether October delivers another 25-basis-point increase as Goldman now expects will determine whether the narrative shifts from "one adjustment" to "sustained tightening."

title: Goldman Sachs reverses Fed call twice in four days, sending ripples through Bitcoin and XRP markets
